population: Hospital newborns with study-specific weight and clinical eligibility
interpretation: Observed mortality depends on setting and follow-up; see both trials.

population: Healthy term dyads intending to breastfeed
interpretation: Neither group was assigned exclusive formula; comparison cannot rank all feeding methods.

population: Very preterm or very low birthweight infants in hospital
interpretation: Lower NEC risk; mortality estimate remains imprecise. Clinical feeding plan required.

population: Eligible infants with severe eczema and/or egg allergy
interpretation: Trial effect depends on entry skin-test stratum. Use formal clinical guidance for first introduction.

comparator: Education; usual family routines remain options
interpretation: Small trial supports more than one choice; feeding, development and safe sleep remain separate.
Effects vary by program and setting; depression needs its own evidence and care pathway.

intervention: Maternal RSVpreF or infant antibody (separate trials)
comparator: Placebo in MATISSE; usual care in HARMONIE
interpretation: The two trials enrolled different populations and used different endpoints and controls. Their efficacy percentages do not compare the products head-to-head. FDA identifies uncertainty about a preterm-birth imbalance. Current gestational window, season and maternal vaccination history matter. No automatic product choice.

US CASCADE found fewer diagnoses over two years; UK BEEP found no clear reduction in eczema present at age two in high-risk infants. Population, duration and outcome definitions differed. BEEP reported increased skin infection rates. The evidence does not support universal product claims or stopping prescribed treatment.

topic: Starting solids with a spoon or self-feeding
interpretation: A supported baby-led program did not clearly improve BMI z scores. Its choking report came from the same families. It could not exclude differences in rare severe events. Gagging and choking require different interpretation. The trial included safety coaching; results cannot establish that a food shape is safe or that an infant with swallowing difficulty is eligible.
